quarterly_data.signal: Navitas + Claros webinar deck: Navitas says the Claros acquisition doubles its SAM to over $8 billion in 2030 (GaN & SiC $3.5 B, SiC JFET $1.0 B, IVR $3.5 B; AI datacenters $5.3 B, grid & energy infrastructure $1.6 B, high performance computing $0.4 B, industrial electrification $0.7 B; page 5 chart, sourced to McKinsey & Company and Navitas). The Claros IVR stack combines a PowerArray digital controller, power FinFETs, NavCoil inductors, NavCap silicon capacitors and an advanced film substrate, with two product paths: packaged IVR (NavPIVR, part CL5003, a 40A chip of 4 x 10A channels) for vertical power delivery and embedded IVR (NavEIVR) integrated into the xPU substrate for embedded power delivery; a 160A chip has 16 x 10A channels and PowerArray scales to 2,560 A (64 x 40A chips) or 10,240 A (64 x 160A chips) (page 14 figure). Navitas describes itself as having pivoted away from consumer to AI infrastructure, with 350M+ units shipped and 450+ patents issued or pending.
quarterly_data.figure: SAM over $8 billion in 2030 (IVR $3.5 B); CL5003 40A chip; PowerArray up to 10,240 A
